text: @local/dsh-mcp-auto-permission 是面向 DSH Web profile 的插件包，加入 Workspace Write + MCP 权限预设，并在该预设启用时处理 MCP 工具的审批请求。它通过 approval/request 钩子识别 mcp__ 前缀的工具，只对当前会话匹配该预设的请求返回一次性允许；其他请求交给后续处理者。插件还提供自动批准状态查询，并在该模式下加入系统提示说明。适合希望减少 MCP 工具逐次确认的 DSH 用户；非 MCP 请求仍走原流程。

@local/dsh-mcp-auto-permission adds a Workspace Write + MCP preset to DSH. In this mode, MCP tools prefixed mcp__ receive allowed-once through the approval hook; other requests continue normally. The plugin also exposes an auto-approval check and adds a matching system prompt note.
让 DSH 在指定权限模式下自动通过 MCP 工具的审批请求。
不想每次调用 MCP 工具都弹审批，能按当前会话模式处理吗？
Can DSH skip approval prompts for MCP calls in a chosen permission mode?
该插件提供「按模式自动批准 MCP 请求」功能：当前会话使用指定预设且工具名以 mcp__ 开头时，approval/request 钩子返回 allowed-once；其他请求交给后续处理器。
该插件提供「MCP 模式提示与状态查询」功能：向其他插件提供 autoApproves 查询，并在目标预设生效时向系统提示加入 MCP 调用预先获批的说明。

@local/dsh-mcp-auto-permission README · dsh-mcp-auto-permission：A DeepSeek Harness bundle that adds the **Workspace Write + MCP** permission preset (`workspace-write-mcp`) and auto-approves MCP approval requests while that preset is current.

@local/dsh-mcp-auto-permission README · Abstract：The harness asks for approval on every tool call unless a permission preset says otherwise. This bundle adds one preset with the `workspace-write` sandbox and the usual approvals for non-MCP tools, plus a plugin that claims `mcp__*` approval requests as `allowed-once`. It changes no tool, no sandbox, and no hard deny: it only answers approval requests.

@local/dsh-mcp-auto-permission README · Behaviour：| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Sandbox | `workspace-write` |
| Approval policy | `ask` |
| Non-MCP tools | unchanged, including sandbox-escalation prompts |
| MCP tools | approval requests claimed as `allowed-once` |
| Preset key | `workspace-write-mcp` |
| Display label | Workspace Write + MCP |

@local/dsh-mcp-auto-permission README · Behaviour：The preset keeps the `workspace-write` file and shell boundary. A tool that the policy hard-denies before asking is still denied; this bundle only answers approval requests, it does not override a deny.

@local/dsh-mcp-auto-permission README · Why an approval hook：A local policy can ask for a tool through `ctx.approval.request`. A profile plugin can claim that request on the `approval/request` waterfall and return `allowed-once`, so the user never sees an approval card. This avoids changing the policy plugin and avoids competing in the `tools/execute` hook, where a later policy listener could still block the call.

@local/dsh-mcp-auto-permission README · Why an approval hook：The hook is scoped by the session's current permission preset. If the preset is not `workspace-write-mcp`, the plugin calls `next()` and the normal answerers decide. It also returns `cancelled` when the request signal is already aborted, and it falls back to the normal answerers when the permission service or projection is unavailable.

@local/dsh-mcp-auto-permission README · Why an approval hook：The plugin provides `mcpAutoPermission.autoApproves(session, toolName)`. A notification plugin can read it to skip a false "approval required" alert for a call that this plugin claims. The approval is still logged and the tool still runs.

A short system-prompt note is active only in this mode. It tells the model that `mcp__*` calls are pre-approved, which prevents generic browser-approval wording from making the model pause.

@local/dsh-mcp-auto-permission README · Install：```sh
DSH_HOME=${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}
git clone https://github.com/ThomasTZh/dsh-mcp-auto-permission \
  "$DSH_HOME/local-plugins/dsh-mcp-auto-permission"
```

Add to `$DSH_HOME/profiles/web/package.json`:

```json
"@local/dsh-mcp-auto-permission": "link:<absolute path to $DSH_HOME>/local-plugins/dsh-mcp-auto-permission"
```

and list `@local/dsh-mcp-auto-permission` in `dsh.profile.bundles`. Install the profile dependencies and restart DSH:

@local/dsh-mcp-auto-permission README · Install：```sh
cd "$DSH_HOME/profiles/web" && pnpm install
```

The bundle patch is applied before the profile patch. If the user later selects a new-session default, the settings service writes a complete `permission` entry into the profile patch, which then overrides the bundle's copy with the same preset definitions. That is ordinary DSH settings persistence.
